title: VIPCare: Virtual Predictive Care workflow with EHR integrated surveillance for optimalfollow-up care management for Cancer Patients
text:
Oncology workforce growth is not keeping pace with the exponential growth in the cancer survivor population in
the US. This plus the complexity of care coordination has led to poor tracking and monitoring of patients in follow-
up care, post-treatment surveillance and long-term survivorship. This project will validate a software tool that
supports providers by automatically tracking cancer patients in follow-up care so that patients are not lost-to-
follow-up and are supported through follow-up care for better outcomes and efficient use of clinic resources.

title: Single cell analysis of the kinome
text:
Kinases are important regulators of biochemical processes in cells. In this project, we propose to
develop single cell tools to profile kinases in the mouse and human brain to examine pathways
involved in aging and Alzheimer’s Diseases. The cell type specific kinases pathways identified
could lead to new targets for therapy.

title: Vevo F2 for High Frequency Ultrasound for Biomedical Imaging at Purdue University
text:
High-resolution ultrasound imaging is critical for understanding disease mechanisms and evaluating new
therapies in preclinical models of cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, gastrointestinal, and cancer biology. This
proposal seeks to upgrade our current ultrasound system to the Vevo F2, enabling enhanced imaging
performance, expanded research applications, and improved data quality that will support biomedical research
aimed at improving public health.

title: Developing Selective-Dissociation for Proteoform Characterization in Top-Down Proteomics
text:
Proteoforms are the primary actors that control most of the chemical processes
underlying biology. Characterizing proteoforms is necessary to understand the
core mechanisms responsible for both health and disease and is the first step
towards identifying treatment options. This proposal will develop a novel method
that will enable rational identification and characterization of proteoforms utilizing
mass spectrometry.

title: Cytokinesis and the Septin Cytoskeleton
text:
Cytokinesis and the septin cytoskeleton play essential roles in cell proliferation and differentiation and are
required for the survival of all organisms. Defects in cytokinesis or septins cause lethality or serious
diseases including cancer, infertility, and neurodegenerative diseases. Thus, mechanistic study of
cytokinesis and the septin cytoskeleton is important not only for understanding basic biology but also for
developing new strategies to treat human diseases.

title: Statistical Methods for Addressing Disease Under-diagnosis Using Electronic Health Record Data
text:
Under-diagnosis occurs when an individual living with a medical condition has not
been diagnosed. Overlooking of diagnosis prevents patients from opportunities of
appropriate treatments and prevention strategies, and often is more serious in some
population subgroups. Recent emphasis on electronic health records (EHRs)
provides a unique opportunity for addressing under-diagnosis, which to date
remains largely unexploited due to lack of suitable analytical methods. The
overarching goal of this project is to develop data-driven methods to accurately
identify patients from EHRs who possibly miss their diagnosis and provide insights
for reasons of under-diagnosis.

title: IU Clinical Center: Drug Induced Liver Injury Network
text:
Drug induced liver injury (DILI) is a rare but serious problem that can lead to liver failure, transplantation,
death, or chronic liver disease. Drug induced liver injury network (DILIN) was set up by the National Institutes
of Health in 2003 to facilitate clinical, mechanistic and therapeutic research related to DILI. Indiana University
is proposing several novel specific aims to promote DILIN during the next funding period.

title: A streamlined base editor reengineering platform to enhance gene editing specificity and selectivity
text:
Base editing technology enables permanent correction of point mutations at their native locus, providing a
potential one-time curative treatment for genetic diseases caused by single-nucleotide substitutions.
Nevertheless, the undesired editing byproducts induced by base editors undermine gene correction efficacy and
pose substantial safety concerns, hindering their clinical translation. This study aims to develop a streamlined
base editor re-engineering platform to guide the evolution of base editors with high precision and defined
selectivity, accelerating the development of therapeutic base editing strategies for diverse genetic diseases, such
as cystic fibrosis.

title: Novel selective allosteric modulators of PTHrP/PTH receptor to inhibit prostate cancer metastases
text:
Every 16 minutes, one man dies of prostate cancer in the United States. Parathyroid hormone
(PTH) receptor type 1 (PTH1R) is the only receptor for PTH-related protein (PTHrP), a well-
known driver for the disease and cancer bone metastases resulting in osteolysis. The goal of
this project is to identify new drug candidates that can effectively block PTH1R overactivity
caused by PTHrP hypersecretion from metastatic prostate cancer cells.

title: Probing the effect of opioids on HIV transcription and latency using a novel dual fluorescent and bioluminescent virus
text:
This proposal will utilize a novel fluorescent and bioluminescent virus called EcoHIV NL4-3 Dual Red to probe
the effects of opioids on HIV proviral transcription and latency reversal in the central nervous system.

title: Hepatoselective Dihydrozuinolizone (HS-DHQ) Molecules for Treatment and Prevention of Hepatitis A Virus (HAV) Infection
text:
Currently, there is no effective antiviral drug available to treat acute hepatitis A. Despite the availability of a
vaccine, hepatitis A virus (HAV) continues to cause thousands of hospitalizations and numerous deaths
annually in the United States and remains a potential bioterrorism threat. Harlingene Life Sciences has
developed a family of hepatoselective (HS) compounds for HAV treatment, demonstrating potent antiviral
activity in vitro and in infected mice and offering the first and only antiviral therapy aimed at mitigating liver
injury in acute hepatitis A.

title: Development of Chimeric Antigen Receptor Phagocytes Against Glioblastoma
text:
Proficiency of macrophages and microglia to infiltrate malignant brain tumors provides a unique
opportunity to exploit their phagocytic properties by engineering the activation of these
professional phagocytes using exogenous expression of Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CARs)
targeted towards a brain tumor-specific antigen.

title: Functions of caldendrin in sensory neurons
text:
In this proposal we will investigate molecular mechanisms controlling the activity of ion channels involved in
touch sensation and how these mechanisms contribute to neurodevelopment and behavior. The impact of our
research on clinical/translational science will be knowledge of pathways that could guide novel diagnostic
and interventional strategies that offset the negative impacts of neurodevelopmental disorders on
individuals and society.

title: Automated methods for standardization and enhancement of metadata in biomedical databases
text:
Biomedical datasets relevant to fundamental biology and human health are increasingly deposited in
centralized databases, enabling opportunities to train powerful machine learning models and perform
large-scale meta-analyses. Unfortunately, poor metadata in biomedical databases is currently a barrier to these
opportunities and thus there is a critical need for metadata curation. We will develop machine learning
methodologies for automated standardization and enhancement of biomedical metadata, allowing the
information contained within centralized biomedical databases to be used to the fullest extent possible.

title: Systematically screening and validating drug repurposing candidates for Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
text:
New drugs developed to target Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (AD/ADRD) have a
99% failure rate; however, drug repurposing--identifying new uses for existing drugs--offers an
alternative approach that can reduce the time, costs, and risks of failure associated with new drug
development. The lack of systematic and readily deployable approaches to screen and validate
drug repurposing candidates represents a critical barrier to the success of leveraging existing
public knowledge and clinical data for the advancement of AD/ADRD treatment and prevention.
We propose combining big data with advanced informatic technologies and computational
capabilities to develop and share tools which systematically screen, prioritize, and validate drug
repurposing candidates and their combinations for AD/ADRD.

title: Predicting early adverse outcomes and discovering biomarkers of treatment toxicity versus treatment response in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma treated with immunotherapy
text:
Immunotherapy is revolutionizing the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma in a vulnerable patient population
with cirrhosis, an end-stage liver disease. Despite its clear benefits at the population level, there are currently
no tools to effectively assess an individual patient’s risk of adverse outcomes from immunotherapy, including
immune-related toxicities, weighed against the potential therapeutic benefits. This proposal aims to address
this gap by leveraging a large longitudinal research cohort and discovering novel biomarkers, ultimately
enabling personalized risk/benefit stratification tools for the application of immunotherapy in hepatocellular
carcinoma to improve patient outcomes by accurately identifying those who are most likely to benefit from
treatment with the least risk.

title: Fully Quantitative Low-Dose, Motion-Resolved Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI in Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma
text:
This project is to develop and validate low-dose quantitative dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) magnetic
resonance imaging (MRI) of the pancreas under free-breathing conditions. This will be accomplished by
cultivating a new technology, DCE MR Multitasking, which can quantify tissue kinetic and flow parameters
even in moving organs. The resulting technology will offer clinicians and investigators a valuable tool to
diagnose, monitor, and study pancreatic and other cancers.

title: Immune control by GBPL proteins in Arabidopsis
text:
Cellular defense protects individual cell against infection across all three domains of life. This proposal focuses
on a new group of host immune proteins - the Guanylate Binding Protein-Like (GBPL) GTPases - in plant
immunity. By employing cutting-edge techniques and interdisciplinary approaches, our efforts have the potential
to unveil novel host defense mechanisms and should have broad implications for the development of innovative
strategies for controlling infectious diseases in both plants and animals.

title: Promoting regenerative repair of aged cartilage
text:
As people age they lose the ability to heal from injuries or diseases like osteoarthritis, partially due to a reduced
ability of old stem cells to differentiate and an inhospitable tissue environment that no longer supports repair. To
address this, we propose to 1) activate SIRT6, a sirtuin that can epigenetically reverse age-associated changes
in stem cells and 2) inhibit apoptosis signal regulating kinase 1 (ASK1), a protein associated with cell death and
inflammation, in the tissue environment. We will test the ability of this novel dual strategy to enhance stem cell
differentiation and promote a more regenerative tissue environment in articular cartilage defect models of aged
animals.

title: Mechanisms underlying constitutive heterochromatin formation at human centromeres
text:
More than half of the human genome consists of repetitive sequences, which must be silenced by
heterochromatin to ensure genome stability. This project will uncover and dissect previously unrecognized
epigenetic mechanisms that involve non-catalytic enzymatic domains or RNA to regulate heterochromatin in
humans. A deeper understanding of how heterochromatin is formed and maintained to repress repetitive
sequences is essential for targeting and correcting aberrant activation of repeats in repeat-associated diseases
including certain cancers, neurodegenerative disorders, and developmental syndromes.
